correctness.rationale: For a one-dimensional graph, each descending link is a discrete set; exactly one earlier neighbor produces a matched vertex-edge arc. Exhausting 720 vertex orders gives 85 distinct gradient masks; maximal masks equal exactly the three 12-member automorphism orbits given in RESULT.md, producing face vector \((18,66,24)\). Each 2-simplex has an edge incident to no other triangle, so 24 explicit elementary collapses leave a connected graph with 18 vertices and 42 edges, hence integral \(H_1\cong\mathbb Z^{25}\) and wedge-of-25-circles homotopy. The signed chain traces in degrees 0–2 are verified for all 12 automorphisms, and the exact Lefschetz character is 24δ_identity+sign. This equals two regular representations plus the S3 sign line. All enumerations and free-face checks were actually executed from the standalone verify.py in this package. Finite exhaustive verification proves this fixed finite claim; no result for other graphs is inferred.

originality.rationale: The foundational full text defines the full strong matching complex and handles paths, cycles, stars, simplices and their boundaries; its scope and text search do not include the triangular prism. The closest published same-graph result computes mod-two homology of the different ordinary Morse complex, whose faces include many Morse matchings not arising from strong vertex filtrations. The new exact integral graph-spine classification and full prism-group rational homology character are not logically implied by that ordinary result. The finite result remains subject to an explicit unindexed-literature risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed, differently named, or subsequently posted calculation of this exact small strong matching complex may exist; lack of a search hit is not proof of global uniqueness.
The character is proved over rationals and does not assert an integral direct-sum decomposition or an equivariant wedge equivalence.
No independent mathematical audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The unfilled triangular prism is the smallest natural cubic prism and lies beyond the graph families classified in the foundational strong-gradient-complex paper. Its completely determined integral homotopy type and full rational prism-automorphism representation are motivated exact topological invariants, not an arbitrary slice. The ordinary Morse complex of precisely the same graph has published mod-two homology in degree four, while the strong complex collapses to circles, demonstrating a substantive contrast caused by the strong-gradient restriction. The 24 explicit collapses and complete G-character provide reusable comparative data; no downstream theorem or all-prism conjecture is claimed.
